insights.summary: Q2 FY27 was another record: revenue ₹2,529 Cr (up 145% year on year, 32% on the quarter), operational EBITDA ₹685 Cr at a 27.1% margin, and PAT ₹517 Cr (reported EBITDA of ₹846 Cr includes a ₹161 Cr US tariff refund). Open order book is a record ₹35,274 Cr, with ₹3,021 Cr scheduled for Q3. Management raised the FY29 EBITDA margin target to about 30% from 27% and kept FY29 revenue at ₹20,000 Cr.

what_changed.text: Margin intent: at or above Q2's 27.1% from Q3 (July guide was 23% by Q4)
New 5-year agreement worth up to $1.2 billion with a second hyperscaler; H1 order intake ₹32,000 Cr
FY29 revenue ₹20,000 Cr; capex ₹1,000 Cr a year; data centres 50% of FY27 revenue
Attach rate hit 24% in H1 (aim was above 20%); now chasing 25%+

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: If Q1 was historic, Q2 has raised the bar again.

analyst_questions.topic: Why raise margin but not revenue?
analyst_questions.answer: Driven by the ₹35,000 Cr order book, richer data-centre mix and attach rate; revenue target stays and will be reviewed as capacity and execution move.
Will aim to match or beat Q2; no new number for the full year.
Hyperscalers still funding from balance sheets; power contracts run to 2031-32; execution delays from land, power and water are likely 'from time to time'.
Does not comment on prices; raw-material supply (germanium, helium) has improved and utilisation is rising each quarter; no numbers shared.

red_flags.text: Reported EBITDA and PAT include a ₹161 Cr one-time US tariff refund; a small further refund is pending.
₹49 Cr impairment on Speedon Networks and higher depreciation; interest up 15% on prepayment penalties.
Payable days fell sharply and working capital rose slightly as suppliers tightened terms.
Order book heavily weighted to two hyperscaler contracts (about $2.3 billion combined); delivery depends on customers' build schedules.

watch_next: Q3 revenue at or above the ₹3,021 Cr scheduled from the order book
Operational EBITDA margin holding 27% or higher
Net finance cost falling from Q3
Data-centre share moving from 33% in H1 towards 50% for the year

business_snapshot.revenue_mix: H1 FY27: data centres 33%; North America 61%, Europe 21%, rest of world 18%
